# Master to Blender Scene and Cut Sketches

## 1 · Resolve the Scene and the Available Tools

Continue the same MOVIOLA directing task through local 3D preparation.

- Keep the resolved Project, Draft, Scene and intended Cut IDs together. The Scene owns an independent editable .blend source; each Cut owns its setup and chosen Sketch. Reuse asset revisions across Scenes, and start a recurring location in an independent working copy.
- Inspect the tools actually advertised by this MOVIOLA connection and the local Blender connection. Remote tools own server state and selection; the local connection owns assembly, camera application and rendering. A loaded skill does not install Blender or add MCP tools.
- Use get_scene_3d_state with the explicit draft_id and sceneId to read the saved mode, currentRevisionId and references checked against current inputs. A saved get_scene projection alone does not prove freshness. set_scene_3d_mode selects 2d or 3d without starting generation; do not mutate scene3d through update_scene. Both recommend and advanced profiles expose these operations. Source connection issuance, revision listing/selection and upload receipts are available in both profiles. Cut setup listing/selection, render connection issuance, candidate image reads and explicit Sketch adoption are also available in both profiles.
- When a local Blender connection is available, use its installed Scene 3D workflow and supported moviola_vcam modules: scene_commands, scene_assets, scene_build, scene_cloud, cut_setup, sketch_capture and sketch_cloud. Resolve their installed inputs rather than copying test fixture destinations or writing substitute transfer logic. If an execution capability is missing, finish the analysis possible with available references and report that step as pending.
- **Choose one execution route per 3D Sketch request before any paid call; the saved 3D mode does not choose it.** Ordinary generate_storyboard here means a call without prepareReferences=true; on a 3D Scene it queues a Mac worker Job. Reference preparation (step 2) is allowed on every route. A session the Mac worker launched — its prompt hands over that queued Generate request and forbids ordinary generate_storyboard — is the worker: it runs the interactive route for its own Scenes and never queues the workflow again. Anywhere else, the interactive route needs all three here: a Blender MCP Python executor in this session, exactly one enabled moviola_vcam resolved as in step 4 whose scene_commands execute("status") returns, and create_scene_source_connection, create_sketch_render_connection and generate_render_sketch on this MOVIOLA connection. If the director chose the Mac worker, or a Job for these Scenes is already queued for it (the director says so, or an earlier call returned its sceneSketch.jobId), take the worker route below. Otherwise, with those three, name the interactive route in one line and run steps 2–6 here without ordinary generate_storyboard for these Scenes, which would queue the same Cuts for a worker.
- The Mac worker route is for a director who chose it and for a Job already queued from the web Editor or an earlier call; follow that Job and do not also work its Cuts here. For a new Job the director's word is the only readiness check — no tool reports a worker before a Job exists — so unless they already said so, have them confirm their worker is running signed in to this same MOVIOLA account and environment; it claims only that account's Jobs. Then call ordinary generate_storyboard with draft_id, the 3D sceneIds and skill_version (plus pipelineMode while unsaved); while the saved inputs are unchanged, the same call for the same Scenes joins a queued Job rather than queueing another. Follow sceneSketch.jobId as step 6 describes.
- With neither the interactive capabilities nor a confirmed worker, do not queue a Job only because this session cannot execute one: nothing would claim it and its Cuts would sit at waiting_for_mac. Name what is missing and let the director choose — connect Blender with the MOVIOLA extension here, start the Mac worker, or switch the Scene to 2D — and report Sketch generation as pending.
- Give each missing piece its own fix, and have the session reopened after any MCP change, because a client fixes its tools when it connects. No MOVIOLA tools: reconnect as https://moviola.vibeproduction.ai/docs#terminal--connect shows. No Blender MCP Python executor: install or update the community MCP for Blender from https://github.com/ahujasid/mcp-for-blender and enable its add-on in Blender. No enabled moviola_vcam: install or enable one; several: leave only one enabled. A ModuleNotFoundError for scene_commands, or Unknown Scene command for a command this page names, means an old extension: stop any take, install the moviola_vcam extension ZIP for this MOVIOLA release with Blender's Install from Disk over the old one, enable it and rerun execute("status").

*The test:* the target is resolved, one execution route is named — or what is missing for both — and every proposed execution step has an available tool or a named handoff.

## 2 · Read the Master as a Space

A single image constrains a useful blockout without determining every hidden surface.

- Inspect the actual Master/Plate images and the saved Scene/Cut direction. Identify the floor and room envelope, openings, dominant landmarks, object groups, depth layers, walking space and the camera view. Separate visible evidence from estimates of scale, occluded objects and the unseen reverse side.
- Review existing references first. For a saved 3D Scene that needs new references, call generate_storyboard with draft_id, the named sceneIds, skill_version and prepareReferences=true under the valid paid authorization. Poll its returned job_id with get_job_status using the same draft_id; repeating the same inputs joins the running Job or returns its completed receipt. A failed Job can be explicitly retried. This prepares Look/Plate/Master without Cut generation, Cut quota reservation or automatic Meshy calls. Ordinary generate_storyboard is the Mac worker route from step 1, never reference preparation. Selected 2D Scenes in a mixed Draft still use the existing server path.
- After preparation, reread get_scene_3d_state and call get_scene_reference_image with draft_id, sceneId, snapshotId and kind=master or plate (look is optional). Inspect the actual returned pixels. Retain identity: Project/Draft/Scene, sourceId, snapshotId, kind, byteLength and sha256. The access URL is only a download location and may expire; it is not the reference identity. The read verifies the bytes against the receipt and reports stale or superseded references. If inputs changed, review the reasons before explicitly preparing a new snapshot; a locally written approved flag does not establish approval.
- Keep the reconstruction choices in the scene recipe: the references used, assumptions about dimensions and unseen layout, Scene instructions and each Cut's visual intent. Resolve uncertainties that would change a requested shot with the director; use stated reversible estimates for ordinary Low blocking.

*The test:* each important spatial choice traces to a visible reference, saved direction or recorded assumption.

## 3 · Reuse Before Modeling

Make only the assets the selected shots need.

Repeated furniture uses instances of one asset; Character proxies keep the Project Character IDs and their visible distinction.
- Before a new paid model, also search the environment-wide shared catalog with search_shared_assets (label text, category, tags); every active account reads the same published Low revisions, whatever its organization. Read the exact one with get_shared_asset_revision and inspect get_shared_asset_preview. Pin revisionId: a published revision never changes, and currentRevisionId only reports a newer one. These reads are free and need no draft_id. They place nothing in Blender; step 4 fetches and places the pinned revision.
- Search also matches searchMetadata, Korean/English labels a vision model read off the preview; a facet it marks unknown, such as material, is not a fact, and labels carry no size: declared dimensions stay the only size. Only the account that published an asset labels it, when the director asks: request_shared_asset_labeling(revision_id, request_id=a fresh UUID, skill_version) is one paid vision request against the Claude quota (quota_blocked once it is spent); poll get_shared_asset_labeling(labeling_id), which is free. A failed run keeps the earlier labels and is never resent by itself; label again with a new request_id. Labeling never changes the GLB or the revision.

It is free and stores a private receipt; get_shared_asset_match(match_id) rereads it. reusable: pin exactly selected.revisionId. insufficient_evidence: show the director the candidates, their previews and the unknown constraints; the director chooses one explicitly or adds requirements (a Mac worker records the object unresolved with insufficient_evidence). no_match: keep its matchId; it is the only basis for a new model. unavailable is not a no-match and never permission to generate; ask again later with the same request_id (a Mac worker records catalog_unavailable). similarity is a model-derived ranking signal, not a probability. A candidate is reused automatically only when the whole description is one of its names; put parts, materials and size that must hold in structure/materials/dimensions, which are proven separately. A named candidate is shown even when its similarity is low.
- Prepare an isolated single-object image only for a missing modeled asset. Inspect the silhouette, complete object bounds, occlusion and baked background/shadow before the generation request. *The test:* every modeled instance pins a published shared revision (or a library revision already pinned), reused or generated once on the server with its match, generation and review receipts and an asset record written before each paid call — or is reported unresolved with its reason. ## 4 · Assemble and Review the Space

Build one coherent room that supports the intended Cut viewpoints.

- For an existing or assembled Blender Scene, call create_scene_source_connection with draft_id and sceneId after setting the Scene mode. Through the existing Blender MCP Python executor, inspect bpy.context.preferences.addons and resolve the enabled module whose final name is moviola_vcam (normally bl_ext.user_default.moviola_vcam). An extension folder on disk does not prove it is enabled; only that list does. If none or several match, resolve the intended enabled extension first. Obtain execute with importlib.import_module(module + ".scene_commands").execute. Use that installed namespace to share the UI/session mutation gate; adding another checkout to sys.path can create a separate gate. Call execute("connect", api_origin=the API origin below, handoff=the returned handoff). It checks the issued connectionId and exact Project/Draft/Scene before storing the scoped grant in local Keychain. Keep the long-lived MOVIOLA token out of Blender files and recipes.
- **api_origin is the server, not the MCP endpoint.** Read this connection's MCP URL from the client's own config, the url alone and never its headers or token: `claude mcp list`, or `codex mcp get moviola --json | jq -r .transport.url`, which honours `$CODEX_HOME`. Keep its scheme://host[:port] and drop the trailing /mcp or /mcp/, so `https://<host>/mcp` gives `https://<host>`. A URL with any other path, a query or credentials does not reduce to an origin; ask. With a work folder the project card's server line must reduce to that same origin; if it does not, the card belongs to another server, so say so and do not connect. Pass the one origin to connect and connect_sketch alike.
- Poll execute("status") until operation.state is completed or failed. Run execute("verify") to recheck live authority, then inspect connection, blenderScene, blendFile and binding. execute("bind") verifies the connection and binds only the selected Blender Scene; it refuses a different existing binding. Save the working .blend explicitly to retain that binding. A busy Scene cannot accept another mutation.
- To assemble from the saved references, call execute("prepare_build", snapshot_id=the current completed snapshotId, cut_ids=the explicit requested Cut IDs, directory=a new local input directory). Poll status, then read input.json and view its Master/Plate files. The scoped server supplies Scene/Cut instructions, Project Character IDs and reference byte identities; changed instructions, stale snapshots or mismatching bytes stop assembly. Read-only execute("find_assets", root=the library directory, label=an optional exact label/category/tag, category=an optional category, tags=a list of required tags) returns available immutable revisions. Select an explicit assetId/revisionId for every modeled placement. For each pinned shared revision call get_shared_asset_revision and get_shared_asset_download (a five-minute link), then execute("fetch_shared_asset", cache=one cache directory kept across builds, api_origin=the same API origin, revision=that revision result, grant=that link result) and poll status for operation.result.cache hit or downloaded; it uses no credential and a verified cached copy needs no new link.
- Create a layout recipe with name, observations, assumptions:{dimensions,occlusion,reverseLayout}, objects, camera and review:{center,distance}. Each object has objectId, kind and worldMatrix; a reused model adds assetId/revisionId (and shared:true for a shared revision), a primitive adds dimensionsMeters and optional color, and a static actor also adds its Project characterId. Camera uses the existing Cut Setup camera schema. Record observed structure separately from each estimate. Server context and references are injected from the prepared input; omit them from this layout recipe.
- Call execute("build_scene", inputs=the prepared directory, recipe=the layout recipe, directory=a new build directory, library=the asset library, shared_cache=that cache when any placement is shared). Poll status; a separate Blender process builds a new working copy without replacing the open file. Repeated assets share one normalized model with distinct stable object IDs. A neutral overhead area light is saved with the source, positioned from the review center and distance; treat it as estimated blockout lighting, not lighting recovered from the Master. For a correction, use another new directory and previous_build=the prior build directory; keep stable IDs and pinned asset revisions. A new asset revision is a separate choice.
- Read execute("get_build", directory=the build directory) and open each images path: master-view, front, side, reverse and top. Compare silhouette, major proportions, openings, landmarks, depth, occlusion and usable Cut camera positions with the actual Master/Plate and Cut instructions. Correct the recipe before publishing. Then call execute("review_build", directory=the build directory, notes={landmarks,depth,occlusion,cutCameraSpace}), with specific nonempty review observations for each key. This records the agent’s visual review against the exact recipe, images and package; local flags never establish server reference identity.
- For a reviewed assembly call execute("publish_build", directory=the build directory). Poll status until operation.result.status=complete and check get_scene_source_upload using the returned requestId. Publication rechecks the saved inputs and uses the original expected source revision. Restore that returned revision before framing Cuts; the prepublication working copy remains unchanged. The recipe, observed/estimated structure, reference identities and correction lineage are embedded in the published .blend.
- For a manually edited, bound Scene, call execute("publish", directory=a new local directory) and retain the returned receipt path. Poll status and confirm operation.result.status=complete, then read get_scene_source_upload with the original requestId on the same draft_id/sceneId. Only the server receipt proves publication; local save, accepted work and uploaded bytes do not. A completed operation with selectionCurrent=false belongs to the previous selection and does not update the newly selected Blender Scene.
- Use list_scene_source_revisions to inspect published revisions and currentRevisionId; includePending=true additionally reports incomplete publications and pointer conflicts. To change the server selection, call select_scene_source_revision with an explicit revisionId and the currentRevisionId just read as expectedCurrentRevisionId. A conflict requires rereading and reconciling the choice, not automatically resubmitting.
- For a historical working copy, call execute("restore", revision_id=the chosen published revision, directory=a new local directory), poll status, and inspect workingCopy. It validates package bytes and dependencies in an isolated Blender process. execute("open") opens that verified copy in a separate Blender process, preserving current work. Downloading a version does not select it on the server.
- After response loss or restart, reconnect to the original Scene, then execute("retry", receipt=the saved publish.json path). The original target, requestId, manifest and expected revision stay fixed; the server receipt is checked before any upload retry. Keep files on grant expiry/revocation, destination mismatch, current revision conflict or integrity failure. Reconnect or reconcile the specific error before continuing; never send the saved request to another Scene.

*The test:* the reviewed space is recoverable from the published package and has a returned source revision.

## 5 · Frame from Saved Editor Intent

The render is the camera and composition reference for the AI Sketch.

- Plan all requested Cut cameras together. Keep a distinct named camera and stable object ID per Cut in the same Scene .blend, using saved Editor lens and framing. Add cameras before publishing the working source, then save each Cut setup against its own camera. Reuse those cameras and the same Scene/assets for sequential capture/register/generate work; do not rebuild the Scene, overwrite one shared camera for every Cut, or wait for human review between Cuts. Local camera creation/rendering makes no provider call.
- Use get_cut_framing_input with draft_id, sceneId and cutId to read the saved shotSize, cameraAngle, composition, focusSubject, lensType, cameraMovement and visible action with inputDigest and published object IDs. Read list_cut_setups for the selected setup, actual camera manifest and framing choices. Open the verified working copy of the exact source revision. An old setup may be applied through execute("apply_setup", revision_id=the setup ID, cut_id=cutId), which restores the baseline before absolute overrides; test A→B→A. Application alone does not certify that setup against new Editor input. To change the saved selection, use select_cut_setup with selection={schemaVersion:1, setupRevisionId, expectedSetupRevisionId:the just-read current ID or null}; resolve a source mismatch before selecting.
- Call execute("prepare_framing", cut_id=cutId, directory=a new input directory), poll status, then execute("get_framing", inputs=the returned framingInputs path). Inspect the actual Scene objects, worldBounds and camera. Resolve focusSubject to published focusObjectIds. Derive numeric camera worldMatrix, projection, lensMm or orthoScale, shift and raster from those dimensions and the saved Cut intent. For each of shotSize, cameraAngle, composition, subjects, lens and staticMoment, explain which actual target/camera choices satisfy it; record assumptions separately. A preset name or forwarded cutInstructions is not a framed Cut. If targets are ambiguous, instructions conflict or the source lacks the required view, name what must be clarified or corrected in Editor/the Scene before continuing.
- Interpret cameraMovement as one named staticMoment of the still. clipCameraMovement belongs to Animatic; keep it out of this framing decision. Call execute("frame_cut", inputs=the prepared path, camera=the numeric camera, framing={inputDigest, focusObjectIds, choices:{shotSize,cameraAngle,composition,subjects,lens,staticMoment}, assumptions}). Inspect the applied camera and blocking. Then call execute("save_setup", cut_id=cutId, directory=a new receipt directory, expected_setup_revision_id=the currentSetupRevisionId just read, including null). Poll until the server receipt is complete. On a conflict reread and resolve the new intent; keep the saved request unchanged.
- Call execute("capture_sketch", directory=a new capture directory) after resolving unsaved source/camera changes. execute("get_sketch", directory=the capture) exposes the PNG and frozen registration intent. Use create_sketch_render_connection, then execute("connect_sketch", api_origin=the same API origin, handoff=the full result). execute("register_sketch", directory=the capture) and poll status. Retain Project/Draft/Scene/Cut, inputDigest, source/setup revisions, renderId, requestId and PNG digest. The render grant remains scoped to local render work; it cannot authorize paid generation.
- Read list_sketch_renders to confirm the exact uploaded renderId and current setup. Visual review is optional for the first pass: do not require six written assessments or pause for per-Cut approval before generating. If the director requests a review, inspect get_sketch_render_image and get_sketch_render_reviews, then record honest observations with stage_sketch_review/review_sketch; do not fabricate passing assessments to start generation.
- A setup with manual is the director's hand-set camera: its manifest camera applies as saved, and manual.input is the Editor direction saved when it was set. It has no framing choices, is not an AI framing, and its numbers never become shot size, lens type or other Editor fields. While it is the current setup without reasons, Generate reuses it: for that Cut do not prepare_framing, frame_cut, save_setup or select another setup, and do not publish a new source revision for its Scene. Reuse a complete render of that setup, or apply_setup it and capture/register a new render. If its reasons show an earlier Editor direction or source, Generate stops with manual_camera_stale; ask whether the director will set the camera again or reset it. save_setup with framing over it is refused with manual_camera_selected. Only when the director explicitly asks to reset framing to Editor, call reset_cut_framing with reset={schemaVersion:1, expectedSetupRevisionId:the just-read current ID}. It keeps every setup and render as history and makes no paid call; the next Generate frames that Cut from the saved Editor intent.
- Editor-only changes invalidate earlier framing even when source/setup IDs are unchanged. After a restart reread get_cut_framing_input. For a setup without manual, an editor_input_changed reason requires fresh prepare_framing → frame_cut → save_setup → capture_sketch → register_sketch. Keep prior renders as history. Recover lost registrations from the saved capture receipt in the original Scene.

*The test:* the current saved Editor digest, concrete camera setup and registered rendered pixels are linked; a visual-review receipt is optional.

## 6 · Complete the First Sketch Automatically

One authorized workflow continues through render-reference generation and first board placement.

- **Before each generate_render_sketch call, write its record.** It is one nonsecret JSON object, `{"apiOrigin":"…","projectId":"…","draftId":"…","sceneId":"…","cutId":"…","renderId":"…","request":{…},"jobId":null,"result":null}`: apiOrigin is the API origin Blender connected to (the capture manifest.json apiOrigin), and request is the exact request object you send; skill_version travels beside it as the current version and is not part of the request's identity. With a work folder the record is one line `Sketch 생성 요청: <record>` under `아직 안 한 것` in that Scene's section of the target Draft's own plan. Each change to it — the line before the call, jobId on the response, result once the Job settles — is a fresh reread, an edit of that line alone and put_work_file of the whole file in the same step, so the server's copy holds the request whichever side a later sync keeps. Without a folder it is generation-<requestId>.json beside registration.json in that render's capture directory. jobId is the response's job_id. result stays null until the Job completes or fails, then becomes {status, selection:selection.status, candidateId:candidate.cutImageId} or its error. When the call answers generation_in_progress instead, this request was never accepted: write "hold":"generation_in_progress" into the record the same way, and follow the Job it names as below without writing that Job's jobId here. Identities are IDs — renderId, jobId and candidateId; the record holds no token, handoff code, grant or image URL.
- Within the existing paid authorization for the named Cuts, continue immediately after each render registration: write the record, then call generate_render_sketch with draft_id, sceneId, cutId, renderId, skill_version and request={schemaVersion:1, requestId:a fresh UUID, selectIfEmpty:true}. Omit reviewId on the normal first pass; never require per-Cut review, generation confirmation or adoption. The Project Sketch model/style uses the render as the primary composition reference and Master/Character as appearance references. Upload-only grants cannot authorize paid generation; use the authenticated MOVIOLA MCP seat under the user-authorized workflow.
- Keep each job_id. The server finishes accepted provider jobs in the background, including after restart; get_job_status reports progress and selection.status. selected means the first Sketch was placed on the board; preserved means an existing selection, changed inputs or access prevented automatic placement.
- **After a restart or a lost response, resolve every record whose result is null before any new paid call.** Its apiOrigin, Draft, Scene and Cut must be the ones this connection reaches. Then, in order: (1) with a jobId, read get_job_status. (2) Without one, read list_sketch_renders for the Cut; an activeGeneration carrying the record's requestId and renderId is that request still running — record its jobId and follow it. (3) Otherwise read list_sketch_candidates, and for each candidate whose inputRenderId is the record's renderId call get_job_status with its imageMetadata.jobId: the one whose requestId is the record's is the result whose response was lost, and a refused one may be this request seen from another account. The render's other candidates are separate deliberate attempts: each is claimed only through its own record, and one no record claims is reported as unclaimed — never a reason to generate or adopt. (4) Only when none of these names it, the record carries no hold, and the director has confirmed this connection signs in as the account that recorded it, resend the identical recorded request — same renderId, same request. Request IDs belong to one account: the same request from another account is a new paid Job. If the server already holds the request, the replay returns its Job and charges nothing again; if it never arrived, this is its first charge, under the original authorization. A generation_in_progress answer holds the record as above.
- A record stays **unresolved** — reported with its reason, its result left null — when its target is not one this connection reaches, when get_job_status refuses its Job or a Job of its render's candidates (it answers only the requesting account, in the Job's original Draft), and while its Job waits with waitingReason submission_unknown (nextAction reconcile_generation), which is reconciled and never resubmitted under any request ID. A held record is different from a lost response: it is known never to have been accepted, so report it as held and never resend it on its own — not even after the Job that held the Cut finishes; it folds away once the director decides. With no record at all, follow any activeGeneration, report the board's Sketch (list_sketch_renders currentSketchInputRenderId names its render) and the candidates list_sketch_candidates shows, and report that Cut as unresolved; recovery reads and starts nothing. A recovered result keeps the selection it got: a preserved candidate waits for an explicit adoption. Another paid attempt comes only from the director's new instruction, as a new requestId with its own record, reported as a new generation.
- On the Mac worker route, poll sceneSketch.jobId with get_job_status and read status first, never a Cut count. completed — granted only after the server verifies a completed AI Sketch receipt for every requested Cut — and failed, with its error, are final whatever stage still says. While the Job is active, report its stage: waiting_for_mac (queued, or the worker stopped renewing its claim), then preparing_scene, rendering and generating_sketches. paused carries the worker's error: report it, and once the director has checked it, the same ordinary generate_storyboard call (or Generate in the web Editor) resumes that Job rather than starting a new paid run. Then read each Cut's result as below.
- A Cut's Job may also have started on the web or in VCam. generate_render_sketch then returns generation_in_progress with activeGeneration {jobId, requestId, renderId, status}: follow that Job with get_job_status (same account) or list_sketch_candidates, and do not start another paid request for the Cut. VCam generates and adopts only through the Sketch connection the director issues on the web; never create or request that code for them. Its Jobs and adoption receipts belong to the issuing account, so recover them with the same request IDs as your own.
- After the first pass, read the board and list_sketch_candidates, and inspect actual output with get_sketch_candidate_image. Report completed Cuts and visible limitations together; the director reviews the finished first Sketches, not intermediate checklists. Camera provenance does not guarantee pixel-perfect composition. Fix a wrong view in Blender and regenerate only the requested Cuts. Additional paid attempts require authorization beyond the existing run.
- Regeneration preserves an existing Sketch. To replace it after comparison, call adopt_sketch_candidate with the exact candidateId and request={schemaVersion:1, requestId:a fresh UUID, expectedPriorSketch:the just-read currentSketch.imageUrl or null}. This free selection step is for replacements or recovered candidates, not a prerequisite for initial production. Keep conflict receipts and reread competing choices rather than overwriting them.
- For adoption response loss use get_sketch_candidate_adoption with the same candidateId/requestId, or resend the identical adoption request. Then reread list_sketch_candidates and inspect currentSketch.candidateId through get_sketch_candidate_image. That reads the selected AI Sketch even when a Final exists; get_cut_image/get_scene_board may prefer Final. An old adopted receipt proves that request completed, not that it remains selected. Keep receipts and images on revoked permission, moved/deleted Cuts or changed source/setup; resolve the reported scope without retargeting old requests.
- Legacy raw-render selections and adoption receipts remain readable with get_sketch_adoption; adopt_sketch_render only replays an existing receipt. New raw selection still returns render_reference_generation_required: Blender pixels are the input, never the AI Sketch output. The normal flow is saved Editor direction → Cut camera → registered render → generate_render_sketch → first board placement. The local worker executes this workflow for queued 3D Cuts; use the bound render path instead of aiDerivation.

*The test:* every requested Cut has an AI Sketch on its initially empty board slot with render/input/source/setup lineage, or a named pending, failed, preserved or unresolved result. Existing Sketches require an explicit replacement choice.

## 7 · Stop at the Requested Stage

A Sketch deliverable is complete without a phone.

- For a Sketch-only request, report the stored Scene revision, adopted Cut Sketches, assumptions and unresolved work. Finalize is optional and needs separate visual comparison when requested; matching provenance does not prove the AI preserved composition. VCam recording and Take upload belong to the later Animatic task. Speech to World and higher asset tiers remain separate work.

Complete when: Each 3D Sketch request followed exactly one route — interactive here, or a Mac worker Job read by status and stage — or was reported pending with the missing capability named; no Job was queued for a worker nobody confirmed. On a finished route the Scene package is published and restorable, and the authorized first pass produces AI Sketches on empty board slots without intermediate review/adoption stops. Every modeled object was reused from a published revision, or generated once on the server, reviewed from its renders and published, then fetched by exact revision — or reported unresolved with its reason; nothing fell back to local Meshy. Every paid asset call had its asset record written before it went out, and a restart resumed each record without a new isolation or charge. Every generate_render_sketch request had its record written before it went out, and every lost response was resolved from that record to its own Job or candidate, or reported unresolved, without a new paid request. Report pending, failed, preserved or unresolved results accurately. No Finalize or VCam step is required.
